\subsection{Novel Optimal Design}

For each round $t$, let $\tilde{a}_{t}=\argmax{k\in[K]}x_{k,t}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}_{t-1}$
denote the arm drawn by the Thompson Sampling algorithm where $\tilde{\beta}_{t-1}\sim N(\widehat{\beta}_{t-1},V_{t-1}^{-1})$
and $\widehat{\beta}_{t-1}$ is the proposed estimator and $V_{t-1}$
is the Gram matrix. Let $\Xb_{t}=[X_{1,t},\cdots,X_{K,t}]\in\RR^{d\times K}$
denote a concatenated context matrix and $\rho_{t}:=\rank(\Xb_{t})$
denote its rank. It is obvious that $\rho_{t}\le\min\{d,K\}$. Applying
reduced QR decomposition, there exists a matrix with orthonormal column
vectors $\Qb_{t}\in\RR^{d\times\rho_{t}}$ and vectors $r_{1,t},\ldots,r_{K,t}\in\RR^{\rho_{t}}$
\[
\begin{bmatrix}x_{1,t} & \cdots & x_{K,t}\end{bmatrix}=\Qb_{t}\begin{bmatrix}r_{1,t} & \cdots & r_{K,t}\end{bmatrix}.
\]
Let $p_{t}$ denote the G-optimal policy over $\{r_{1,t},\ldots,r_{K,t}\}$.
By Kiefer-wolfwiez theorem, G-optimal design is equivalent with D-optimal
design, which is efficiently computable. By definition of the G-optimal
policy, we have $\max_{k^{\prime}\in[K]}r_{k^{\prime},t}^{\top}(\sum_{k=1}^{K}p_{t}(k)r_{k,t}r_{k,t}^{\top})^{-1}r_{k^{\prime},t}=\rho_{t}$.
Thus, for all $k^{\prime}\in[K]$
\[
(\rho_{t}\sum_{k=1}^{K}p_{t}(k)r_{k,t}r_{k,t}^{\top})^{-1/2}r_{k^{\prime},t}r_{k^{\prime},r}^{\top}(\rho_{t}\sum_{k=1}^{K}p_{t}(k)r_{k,t}r_{k,t}^{\top})^{-1/2}\preceq I_{\rho_{t}},
\]
which implies $r_{k^{\prime},t}r_{k^{\prime},t}\preceq\rho_{t}\sum_{k=1}^{K}p_{t}(k)r_{k,t}r_{k,t}^{\top}$.
Thus, for each $k^{\prime}\in[K]$, 
\[
|x_{k^{\prime},t}^{\top}y|^{2}=|r_{k^{\prime},t}\Qb_{t}^{\top}y|^{2}\le\rho_{t}\sum_{k=1}^{K}p_{t}(k)\big(r_{k,t}\Qb_{t}^{\top}y\big)^{2}=\sum_{k=1}^{K}p_{t}(k)(\sqrt{\rho_{t}}x_{k,t}^{\top}y)^{2}.
\]
Thus, for $k^{\prime}\in[K]$, we obtain $x_{k^{\prime},t}x_{k^{\prime},t}^{\top}\preceq\rho_{t}\sum_{k=1}^{K}p_{t}(k)x_{k,t}x_{k,t}^{\top}$. 

Based on this G-optimal design, we construct a novel exploration scheme
that is compatible with both Thompson Sampling and Doubly Robust estimator.
Define the distribution over $[K]$ as 
\[
\bar{\pi}_{t}(k)=\frac{p_{t}(k)+\II(k=\tilde{a}_{t})}{2}.
\]
Let $\{\bar{a}_{t}^{(n)}:n\ge1\}$ denote the IID samples from the
distribution $\bar{\pi}_{t}$ and let $m_{t}:=\{n\le\lceil\log\frac{\sqrt{t}}{d}/\log2\rceil:\bar{a}_{t}^{(n)}=\tilde{a}_{t}\}$
denote the stopping time when the action from $\bar{\pi}_{t}$ matches
$\tilde{a}_{t}$ with in $\lceil\log\frac{\sqrt{t}}{d}/\log2\rceil$
number of trials. We select the action $a_{t}=\bar{a}_{t}^{(m_{t})}$.
With probability at least $1-d/\sqrt{t}$, the algorithm selects $\tilde{a}_{t}$
while it selects other actions with probability at most $d/\sqrt{t}$.
Let $\Acal_{m}$ denote the sigma-algebra generated by $\{\bar{a}_{t}^{(n)}:n\in[m]\}$.
Given the sigma-algebra $\Acal_{m_{t}^{-}}$ generated by the events
$\cap_{m=1}^{\lceil\log\frac{\sqrt{t}}{d}/\log2\rceil}\{A\cap\{m_{t}=m\}:A\in\Acal_{m-1}\}$,
which is the information right before the matching event, the distribution
of $\bar{a}_{t}^{(m_{t})}$ is $\bar{\pi}_{t}$ which is the mixture
of G-optimal design and the selected arm $\tilde{a}_{t}$. 

Let $v_{1,t},\ldots,v_{\rho_{t},t}$ denote the orthogonal vectors
such that $\frac{1}{2}\sum_{k=1}^{K}\rho_{t}p_{t}(k)x_{k,t}x_{k,t}^{\top}+\frac{1}{2}x_{\tilde{a}_{t},t}x_{\tilde{a}_{t},t}^{\top}=\sum_{i=1}^{\rho_{t}}v_{i,t}v_{i,t}^{\top}$.
Let $i_{t}\sim\text{unif}([\rho_{t}])$ and
\[
X_{a_{t},t}=\begin{cases}
\sqrt{\rho_{t}}x_{a_{t}} & a_{t}\neq\tilde{a}_{t}\\
x_{\tilde{a}_{t},t} & a_{t}=\tilde{a}_{t}
\end{cases},\quad Y_{a_{t},t}=\begin{cases}
\sqrt{\rho_{t}}R_{a_{t},t} & a_{t}\neq\tilde{a}_{t}\\
R_{\tilde{a}_{t},t} & a_{t}=\tilde{a}_{t}
\end{cases}.
\]
\[
\theta_{t}^{R}:=\Gb_{t}^{-1}\sum_{s=1}^{t}Y_{a_{s},s}X_{a_{s},s},
\]
denote the weighted ridge estimator, where the Gram matrix,
\[
\Gb_{t}:=\sum_{s=1}^{t}\big(\frac{1}{2}\sum_{k=1}^{K}\rho_{s}p_{s}(k)x_{k,s}x_{k,s}^{\top}+\frac{1}{2}x_{\tilde{a}_{s},s}x_{\tilde{a}_{s},s}^{\top}\big)+\lambda_{t}I_{d}.
\]
We define the augmented DR estimator
\[
\widehat{\theta}_{t}:=\Gb_{t}^{-1}\sum_{s=1}^{t}\Big(\sum_{i=1}^{\rho_{t}}(1-\frac{\II(i_{s}=i)}{1/\rho_{s}})v_{i,s}v_{i,s}^{\top}\beta_{t}^{R}+Y_{a_{s},s}X_{a_{s},s}\Big),
\]

\begin{thm}
\label{thm:self}(Self-normalized bound for the ADR estimator) Suppose
$t$ satisfies, $t\ge d\log??$. With probability at least $1-\delta$,
\[
\|\widehat{\theta}_{t}-\theta\|_{\Gb_{t}}\le\sqrt{2d\sigma^{2}\log\frac{1}{\delta}},
\]
for all $t\ge??$
\end{thm}

The initialization round is to ensure that the imputation estimator
$\beta_{t}^{R}$ is accurate enough to guarantee augmented estimation
error bound. 
\begin{proof}
By definition,Recall that 
\begin{align*}
\Gb_{t} & :=\sum_{s=1}^{t}\big(\frac{1}{2}\sum_{k=1}^{K}\rho_{s}p_{s}(k)x_{k,s}x_{k,s}^{\top}+\frac{1}{2}x_{\tilde{a}_{s},s}x_{\tilde{a}_{s},s}^{\top}\big)+\lambda_{t}\Ib_{d}
\end{align*}
The definition of $v_{i,s}$ implies $\frac{1}{2}\sum_{k=1}^{K}\rho_{s}p_{s}(k)x_{k,s}x_{k,s}^{\top}+\frac{1}{2}x_{\tilde{a}_{s},s}x_{\tilde{a}_{s},s}^{\top}=\sum_{i=1}^{\rho_{s}}v_{i,s}v_{i,s}^{\top}$
for all $s\in[t]$. Let us write $\eta_{a_{s},s}:=Y_{a_{s},s}-X_{a_{s},s}^{\top}\theta_{\star}$.
By definition of the estimator and the Gram matrix,
\[
\begin{split} & \|\widehat{\theta}_{t}-\theta_{\star}\|_{\Gb_{t}}\\
 & =\Big\Vert\sum_{s=1}^{t}\sum_{i=1}^{\rho_{s}}(1-\frac{\II(i_{s}=i)}{1/\rho_{s}})v_{i,s}v_{i,s}^{\top}(\theta_{t}^{R}-\theta_{\star})+\sum_{s=1}^{t}\eta_{a_{s},s}X_{a_{s},s}+\big(\sum_{s=1}^{t}X_{a_{s}}X_{a_{s}}^{\top}-\Gb_{t}\big)\theta_{\star}\Big\Vert_{\Gb_{t}^{-1}}.
\end{split}
\]
Let us write $\Vb_{t}:=\sum_{s=1}^{t}\sum_{i=1}^{\rho_{s}}\frac{\II(i_{s}=i)}{1/\rho_{s}}v_{i,s}v_{i,s}^{\top}+\lambda_{t}\Ib_{d}$.
Then,
\[
\begin{split} & \|\widehat{\theta}_{t}-\theta_{\star}\|_{\Gb_{t}}\\
 & =\Big\Vert(\Gb_{t}-\Vb_{t})(\theta_{t}^{R}-\theta_{\star})+\sum_{s=1}^{t}\eta_{a_{s},s}X_{a_{s},s}+\big(\sum_{s=1}^{t}X_{a_{s}}X_{a_{s}}^{\top}-\Gb_{t}\big)\theta_{\star}\Big\Vert_{\Gb_{t}^{-1}}.
\end{split}
\]
By definition of $\theta_{t}^{R}=\Gb_{t}^{-1}\sum_{s=1}^{t}Y_{a_{s},s}X_{a_{s},s}$,
\[
\theta_{t}^{R}-\theta_{\star}=\Gb_{t}^{-1}\sum_{s=1}^{t}\eta_{a_{s},s}X_{a_{s},s}+\Gb_{t}^{-1}(\sum_{s=1}^{t}X_{a_{s},s}X_{a_{s},s}^{\top}-\Gb_{t})\theta_{\star}
\]
 It follows that 
\[
\begin{split} & \|\widehat{\theta}_{t}-\theta_{\star}\|_{\Gb_{t}}\\
 & =\Big\Vert(2\Ib_{d}-\Vb_{t}\Gb_{t}^{-1})\big(\sum_{s=1}^{t}\eta_{a_{s},s}X_{a_{s},s}+(\sum_{s=1}^{t}X_{a_{s},s}X_{a_{s},s}^{\top}-\Gb_{t})\theta_{\star}\big)\Big\Vert_{\Gb_{t}^{-1}}\\
 & =\Big\Vert(2\Ib_{d}-\Gb_{t}^{-1/2}\Vb_{t}\Gb_{t}^{-1/2})\Gb_{t}^{-1/2}\big(\sum_{s=1}^{t}\eta_{a_{s},s}X_{a_{s},s}+(\sum_{s=1}^{t}X_{a_{s},s}X_{a_{s},s}^{\top}-\Gb_{t})\theta_{\star}\big)\Big\Vert_{2}.
\end{split}
\]
By definition of the matrix operator norm, $\|M\|_{2}:=\max_{\|x\|_{2}\le1}\|Mx\|_{2}$,
\begin{align*}
 & \|\widehat{\theta}_{t}-\theta_{\star}\|_{\Gb_{t}}\\
 & \le\Big\Vert2\Ib_{d}-\Gb_{t}^{-1/2}\Vb_{t}\Gb_{t}^{-1/2}\Big\Vert_{2}\cdot\Big\Vert\sum_{s=1}^{t}\eta_{a_{s},s}X_{a_{s},s}+(\sum_{s=1}^{t}X_{a_{s},s}X_{a_{s},s}^{\top}-\Gb_{t})\theta_{\star}\Big\Vert_{\Gb_{t}^{-1}}.
\end{align*}
By Lemma ??
\begin{align*}
\Big\Vert2\Ib_{d}-\Gb_{t}^{-1/2}\Vb_{t}\Gb_{t}^{-1/2}\Big\Vert_{2}\le & 1+\Big\Vert\Ib_{d}-\Gb_{t}^{-1/2}\Vb_{t}\Gb_{t}^{-1/2}\Big\Vert_{2}\\
\le & 3.
\end{align*}
Thus, by triangular inequality
\begin{align*}
\|\widehat{\theta}_{t}-\theta_{\star}\|_{\Gb_{t}} & \le3\Big\Vert\sum_{s=1}^{t}\eta_{a_{s},s}X_{a_{s},s}+(\sum_{s=1}^{t}X_{a_{s},s}X_{a_{s},s}^{\top}-\Gb_{t})\theta_{\star}\Big\Vert_{\Gb_{t}^{-1}}\\
 & \le3\Big\Vert\sum_{s=1}^{t}\eta_{a_{s},s}X_{a_{s},s}\Big\Vert_{\Gb_{t}^{-1}}+3\Big\Vert(\sum_{s=1}^{t}X_{a_{s},s}X_{a_{s},s}^{\top}-\Gb_{t})\theta_{\star}\Big\Vert_{\Gb_{t}^{-1}}.
\end{align*}
For $C_{s}>0$ to be determined later, let $\bar{\eta}_{a_{s},s}:=\eta_{a_{s},s}\II(|\eta_{a_{s},s}|\le C_{s})-\EE[\eta_{a_{s},s}\II(|\eta_{a_{s},s}|\le C_{s})]|\Hcal_{s-1}]$
and $\tilde{\eta}_{a_{s},s}:=\eta_{a_{s},s}\II(|\eta_{a_{s},s}|>C_{s})-\EE[\eta_{a_{s},s}\II(|\eta_{a_{s},s}|>C_{s})|\Hcal_{s-1}]$
\[
\Big\Vert\sum_{s=1}^{t}\eta_{a_{s},s}X_{a_{s},s}\Big\Vert_{\Gb_{t}^{-1}}\le\Big\Vert\sum_{s=1}^{t}\bar{\eta}_{a_{s},s}X_{a_{s},s}\Big\Vert_{\Gb_{t}^{-1}}+\Big\Vert\sum_{s=1}^{t}\tilde{\eta}_{a_{s},s}X_{a_{s},s}\Big\Vert_{\Gb_{t}^{-1}}.
\]
By Lemma ??, there exists a martingale differences $\{D_{1,a_{s}},D_{2,a_{s}}:s\in[t]\}$,
such that 
\[
\Big\Vert\sum_{s=1}^{t}\bar{\eta}_{a_{s},s}X_{a_{s},s}\Big\Vert_{\Gb_{t}^{-1}}=\sqrt{\big(\sum_{s=1}^{t}D_{1,a_{s}}\big)^{2}+\big(\sum_{s=1}^{t}D_{2,a_{s}}\big)^{2}},
\]
and $\max\{|D_{1,a_{s}}|,|D_{2,a_{s}}|\}\le\|\bar{\eta}_{a_{s},s}X_{a_{s},s}\|_{\Gb_{t}^{-1}}\le C_{s}\|X_{a_{s},s}\|_{\Gb_{t}^{-1}}$
for all $s\in[t]$. 
\end{proof}
\begin{lem}
Let $A$ denote a random variable sampled from the multinomial distribution
$\pi(k)=\PP(A=k)$ for $k=1,\ldots,m$ and $D_{1},\ldots,D_{m}$ denote
the independent mean-zero random variables such that $|D_{k}|\le1/2$
for all $k=1,\ldots,m$. Suppose further $\EE[D_{A}^{2}]\le L_{2}$.
Then,
\[
\EE[\exp(D_{A}-\sum_{k=1}^{m}\pi(k)D_{k})]\le\exp(4L_{2}^{2}).
\]
 
\end{lem}

\begin{proof}
For a nonnegative random variable $Z$, define the entropy $\Ent(Z)=\EE[Z\log Z]-\EE[Z]\log\EE[Z]$.
By definition 
\begin{equation}
\begin{alignedat}{1} & \Ent\big(\exp(D_{A}-\sum_{k=1}^{m}\pi(k)D_{k})\big)\\
 & =\EE\Big[\big(D_{A}-\sum_{k=1}^{m}\pi(k)D_{k}\big)\exp(D_{A}-\sum_{k=1}^{m}\pi(k)D_{k})\Big]-\EE[\exp(D_{A}-\sum_{k=1}^{m}\pi(k)D_{k})]\log\EE[\exp(D_{A}-\sum_{k=1}^{m}\pi(k)D_{k})].
\end{alignedat}
\label{eq:entD}
\end{equation}
 For $x=(x_{1},\ldots,x_{m})$, define $\psi(x)=\log\sum_{k=1}^{m}\pi(k)e^{x_{k}}$.
Note that $\psi(0)=0$ and $\nabla\psi(0)=\pi$. Let $D=(D_{1},\ldots,D_{m})$.
Then 
\[
\nabla\psi(D)^{\top}D=\frac{\sum_{k=1}^{K}\pi(k)D_{k}e^{D_{k}}}{\sum_{k=1}^{K}\pi(k)e^{D_{k}}}=e^{-\psi(D)}\sum_{k=1}^{K}\pi(k)D_{k}e^{D_{k}}.
\]
Taking expectation over $A\sim\pi$,
\begin{align*}
\EE\Big[\big(D_{A}-\sum_{k=1}^{m}\pi(k)D_{k}\big)\exp\Big(D_{A}-\sum_{k=1}^{m}\pi(k)D_{k}\Big)\Big]= & \EE\Big[\big(\sum_{k=1}^{m}\pi(k)D_{k}e^{D_{k}}-\sum_{k=1}^{m}\pi(k)D_{k}\sum_{k=1}^{m}\pi(k)e^{D_{k}}\big)\exp(-\nabla\psi(0)^{\top}D)\Big]\\
= & \EE\Big[(\nabla\psi(D)^{\top}D-\nabla\psi(0)^{\top}D)e^{\psi(D)-\nabla\psi(0)^{\top}D}\Big]\\
= & \EE\Big[\big(\nabla\psi(D)-\nabla\psi(0)\big)^{\top}De^{\psi(D)-\nabla\psi(0)^{\top}D}\Big].
\end{align*}
By definition of the Bregman divergence $B_{\psi}(a,b)=\psi(a)-\psi(b)-\nabla\psi(b)^{\top}(b-a)$,
it follows that
\begin{align*}
\EE\Big[\big(D_{A}-\sum_{k=1}^{m}\pi(k)D_{k}\big)\exp\Big(D_{A}-\sum_{k=1}^{m}\pi(k)D_{k}\Big)\Big]= & \EE\Big[\big(\nabla B_{\psi}(D,0)^{\top}De^{B_{\psi}(D,0)}\Big],
\end{align*}
where the gradient is applied to the first component of the Bregman
divergence. The remaining terms in \eqref{eq:entD} can be written
as
\begin{align*}
\EE[\exp(D_{A}-\sum_{k=1}^{m}\pi(k)D_{k})] & =\EE\Big[\sum_{k=1}^{m}\pi(k)e^{D_{k}}\exp(-\nabla\psi(0)^{\top}D)\Big]\\
 & =\EE\Big[e^{B_{\psi}(D,0)}\Big].
\end{align*}
Thus,
\begin{align*}
 & \Ent\big(\exp(D_{A}-\sum_{k=1}^{m}\pi(k)D_{k})\big)\\
 & =\EE\Big[\nabla B_{\psi}(D,0)^{\top}De^{B_{\psi}(D,0)}\Big]-\EE\Big[e^{B_{\psi}(D,0)}\Big]\log\EE\Big[e^{B_{\psi}(D,0)}\Big]\\
 & =\Ent(e^{B_{\psi}(D,0)})+\EE[e^{B_{\psi}(D,0)}\big(\nabla B_{\psi}(D,0)^{\top}D-B_{\psi}(D,0)\big)].
\end{align*}
By the representation lemma (Lemma ??) for $u\in\RR$, 
\[
\Ent(e^{B_{\psi}(D,0)})\le\EE[e^{B_{\psi}(D,0)}\big(B_{\psi}(D,0)-u\big)-(e^{B_{\psi}(D,0)}-e^{u})].
\]
Thus,
\begin{align*}
 & \Ent\big(\exp(D_{A}-\sum_{k=1}^{m}\pi(k)D_{k})\big)\\
 & \le\EE[e^{B_{\psi}(D,0)}\big(\nabla B_{\psi}(D,0)^{\top}D-u\big)-(e^{B_{\psi}(D,0)}-e^{u})]\\
 & =\EE[e^{B_{\psi}(D,0)}\big(\nabla B_{\psi}(D,0)^{\top}D-u-1+e^{u-B_{\psi}(D,0)}\big)]
\end{align*}
Let $D^{\prime}$ denote the independent copy of $D$. Setting $u=B_{\psi}(D^{\prime},0)$
and taking expectation on both sides, 
\begin{align*}
 & \Ent\big(\exp(D_{A}-\sum_{k=1}^{m}\pi(k)D_{k})\big)\\
 & \le\EE[e^{B_{\psi}(D,0)}\big(\nabla B_{\psi}(D,0)^{\top}D-B_{\psi}(D^{\prime},0)-1+e^{B_{\psi}(D^{\prime},0)-B_{\psi}(D,0)}\big)].
\end{align*}
By the symmetrization argument, setting $Z:=\nabla B_{\psi}(D^{\prime},0)^{\top}D^{\prime}-B_{\psi}(D,0)$
gives
\begin{align*}
 & \Ent\big(\exp(D_{A}-\sum_{k=1}^{m}\pi(k)D_{k})\big)\\
 & \le\EE[e^{B_{\psi}(D^{\prime},0)}\big(\nabla B_{\psi}(D^{\prime},0)^{\top}D^{\prime}-B_{\psi}(D,0)-1+e^{B_{\psi}(D,0)-B_{\psi}(D^{\prime},0)}\big)].\\
 & =\EE[e^{B_{\psi}(D^{\prime},0)}\big(Z-1+e^{B_{\psi}(D,0)-B_{\psi}(D^{\prime},0)}\big)]\\
 & =\EE[e^{B_{\psi}(D,0)}\big((Z-1)e^{B_{\psi}(D^{\prime},0)-B_{\psi}(D,0)}+1\big)]\\
 & \le\EE[e^{B_{\psi}(D,0)}\big((Z-1)e^{Z}+1\big)],
\end{align*}
where the last inequality uses the fact that $B_{\psi}(\cdot,0)$
is strictly convex and $B_{\psi}(D^{\prime},0)\le\nabla B_{\psi}(D^{\prime},0)^{\top}D^{\prime}.$
Because $\nabla B_{\psi}(D^{\prime},0)^{\top}D^{\prime}\ge0$ and
$B_{\psi}(D,0)\ge0$,
\begin{align*}
|Z|= & |\nabla B_{\psi}(D^{\prime},0)^{\top}D^{\prime}-B_{\psi}(D,0)|\\
\le & \max\{\nabla B_{\psi}(D^{\prime},0)^{\top}D^{\prime},B_{\psi}(D,0)\}\\
\le & \max\{\nabla B_{\psi}(D^{\prime},0)^{\top}D^{\prime},\nabla B_{\psi}(D,0)^{\top}D\}.
\end{align*}
By assumption, $\|\nabla\psi(D^{\prime})\|_{1}=1$ and $\|D^{\prime}\|_{\infty}\le1/2$.
It follows that
\begin{equation}
\nabla B_{\psi}(D^{\prime},0)^{\top}D^{\prime}\le\|\nabla\psi(D^{\prime})-\nabla\psi(0)\|_{1}\|D^{\prime}\|_{\infty}\le1,\label{eq:Z_bound}
\end{equation}
and $|Z|\le1$. Because $(z-1)e^{z}+1\le z^{2}$ for $|z|\le1$, 
\[
\Ent\big(\exp(D_{A}-\sum_{k=1}^{m}\pi(k)D_{k})\big)\le\EE[e^{B_{\psi}(D,0)}Z^{2}]
\]
By definition of $Z$,
\begin{align*}
Z^{2}= & (\nabla B_{\psi}(D^{\prime},0)^{\top}D^{\prime}-B_{\psi}(D,0))^{2}\\
\le & (\nabla B_{\psi}(D^{\prime},0)^{\top}D^{\prime})^{2}+B_{\psi}(D,0)^{2},
\end{align*}
where the inequality holds because $\nabla B_{\psi}(D^{\prime},0)^{\top}D^{\prime}\ge0$
and $B_{\psi}(D,0)\ge0$. For the first term, by the mean value theorem,
there exists $\bar{D}$ such that $\|\bar{D}\|_{\infty}\le1/2$ and
\[
\nabla B_{\psi}(D^{\prime},0)^{\top}D^{\prime}=\|D^{\prime}\|_{\nabla^{2}\psi(\bar{D})}^{2}\le\sum_{k=1}^{m}\frac{\pi(k)e^{\bar{D}_{k}}(D_{k}^{\prime})^{2}}{\sum_{k^{\prime}=1}^{m}\pi(k^{\prime})e^{\bar{D}_{k}}}\le e\sum_{k=1}^{K}\pi(k)(D_{k}^{\prime})^{2}
\]
where the first inequality holds because $\nabla^{2}\psi(\bar{D})=\sum_{k=1}^{m}\eb_{k}^{\top}\nabla\psi(\bar{D})\eb_{k}\eb_{k}^{\top}-\nabla\psi(\bar{D})\nabla\psi(\bar{D})^{\top}$.
Thus, $\nabla B_{\psi}(D^{\prime},0)^{\top}D^{\prime}\le e\EE[(D_{k}^{\prime})^{2}]\le L_{2}$.
Similarly, because $B_{\psi}(\cdot,0)$ is strictly convex,
\[
B_{\psi}(D,0)\le\nabla B_{\psi}(D,0)^{\top}D\le L_{2}.
\]
Thus, $Z^{2}\le2L_{2}^{2}$ and 
\[
\Ent\big(\exp(D_{A}-\sum_{k=1}^{m}\pi(k)D_{k})\big)\le\EE[e^{B_{\psi}(D,0)}]2L_{2}^{2}
\]
By Herbt's method (Lemma ??),
\[
\EE[\exp(D_{A}-\sum_{k=1}^{m}\pi(k)D_{k})]\le\exp(4L_{2}^{2}),
\]
which completes the proof.
\end{proof}
